speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head Q of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Talent and data are, in my opinion, the most basic yet most important success factors.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We need data to innovate and we need people to get things done.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In my Budget debate speech in February 2020, I talked about the need for a high concentration of skilled workers with a critical mass of talents if we are to excel in tech and innovation, like we did in biotech.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Singapore needs to offer an abundance of talents who not only meet existing demands but also attract future unicorns to Singapore from the region and beyond.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Just as importantly, we need to have homegrown unicorns.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We need more Singapore digital leaders and tech unicorns to further cement our position in the world.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: To ensure sustainability and progression in this area, I would like to ask what the Government is doing to actively cultivate digital leaders.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Would the Government consider formally introducing a mentorship programme that attracts top talents and company founders from around the world, perhaps to leverage the TechPass holders, to mentor our youths and start-ups?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I spoke about this in Parliament last year and I raise this again now.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Ultimately, we would want to create a vibrant community of talents, groom the next generation and increase Singapore’s mindshare to further cement Singapore’s position on the global stage.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: An area of keen interest to me is how we are attracting and retaining women in this niche tech space.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In a 2019 Harvard Business Review research paper, it was reported that investing in gender diversity helps create a positive feedback loop in talent attraction and financial gains for a company.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, I would like to ask the Government what are the plans in place to further encourage the entry of women to the tech space.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: In an article by Forbes that outlined one of the benefits for introducing a transparent corporate culture is that it fosters employee happiness and talent retention.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Apart from having a list of IMDA-accredited companies, could there be a more concerted effort to encourage government-linked companies to partner local tech firms and bring them along in overseas ventures?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Without the opportunity to obtain a “big break”, our local start-ups can get stuck in a vicious cycle of small projects.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This inadvertently creates a false impression that our local start-ups are capable of undertaking only small projects.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Moreover, without a sizeable project in Singapore to add to their credential, some local companies may face considerable challenges when venturing overseas, if they were to do so on their own.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And, because of the lack of credibility or credential, local start-ups might be pressured to reduce their fees to secure the contract.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This again creates a downward spiral of giving discounts which is unsustainable in the long run.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Can we pursue big brands less and favour our local companies a bit more?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Could we consider “Support Singapore” measures to prioritise deserving local companies, perhaps those in the Scale-up programme, in certain public project tenders?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Such opportunities could be the break our companies need to launch themselves as Singapore’s next tech unicorn.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And on to my final point on data collection.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: I understand that this is a sensitive topic, but the current highly sensitised climate makes it difficult for local firms to collect data for the purpose of innovating their products or services.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: At times, companies face challenges obtaining data, despite offering assurance that it will be anonymised.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But without data, it could be very difficult for firms to innovate and they risk creating products in a vacuum.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Hence, there is a need to strike a balance in protecting data and enabling data for innovation.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We want to be a global data centre.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: But how could we use data for greater good?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Could the Government consider lending its support as a partner to companies in their research and studies?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: What else could the Government do to strike this balance?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Moreover, going digital breaks down geographical and physical constraints and promises limitless markets and opportunities.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: However, MSMEs often find it daunting to digitalise as they know not the "what" and the "how".

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Neither do they have the technical expertise internally to scan the horizon for the wide array of digital solutions available in the market, nor do they have the resources to engage qualified consultants just to help them digitalise.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: On this note, I would like to suggest three points.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: The first is to build trust in technology. “I don’t know what I don’t know”, “What if I am scammed?”, “Will the bank or agency know my everything?”.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Buy-in amongst MSMEs on the benefits of digitalisation could remain weak.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Absorbed in their daily operations, many MSMEs have little capacity left to care about achieving incremental productivity gain through digitalisation, when one, every day is an existential fight and two, the digital solutions are possibly “alien” to them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Compounded by the occasional stories of how some fall prey to scams, digitalisation can become a mysterious and scary monster.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Could the government share how it is addressing myths and helping MSMEs understand the benefits of digitalisation, so as to engender greater confidence?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Even amongst the more forward-looking MSMEs that believe in digitalisation, they may not afford the time to properly understand the digital specifications, much less to deploy and implement the solutions.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: The business imperative will be strong if digital adoption is shown to increase topline and reduce bottomline.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Of course, Government schemes such as the Start Digital Pack are useful.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: But if I may suggest, it is for the Government to look into implementation details and how application experience can be enhanced.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: This to me an example of a missed opportunity for MSMEs to give digitalisation a shot.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I therefore ask the Ministry to share more about what is done to help MSMEs transform?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Chairman, digital technologies are indisputably relevant to the modern economy.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And this has been particularly so during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As the demand for new spheres of innovation grows to cushion the disruptions and to leverage on new opportunities brought about by the pandemic, new applications, new digital solutions appear on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Digital technologies are increasingly impacting all parts of the economy.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Even in the traditional sectors like F&B, agriculture, and construction, technology investment is growing fast as a worldwide trend.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Asia has been benefiting from the new wave of digital innovation in the recent years.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Compared to the rest of the world, the IMF observed that Asia is leading in e-commerce and fintech.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Both developing and advanced economies in the region have seen significant digital gains.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We must strive to understand how best we can make the most of these digital opportunities to benefit our economy and improve our living standards.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Can the Minister share how we will strengthen our competitive advantage in the global digital economy?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have a significant foothold over our regional counterparts as tech giants flock to us to establish headquarters or regional offices in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But as we heard in the earlier MTI Committee of Supply, the technology talent crunch remains a perpetual concern.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Government and businesses must therefore focus efforts on finding talented individuals to secure our technology start-up status.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It will not be easy as many of the job openings require specialists of digital skills.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How do we therefore ensure that we have sufficient talent to meet the demands of our growing digital economy?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Mr Chairman, over the past one year, many of us have seen our screen-time increase by leaps and bounds.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: My friends in the stockbroking industry tell me that after years of decline, their commissions have gone up.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Data has shown that there have been more trades done, although in small amounts.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And we all know that shopping online is prevalent these days.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Life has indeed changed and the digital world is occupying more of our waking hours.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: How has digitalisation allowed us to ease into the new reality of life during COVID-19?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, please allow me to submit my cuts (e), (f) and (g) together.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: COVID-19 has been a catalyst for business transformation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: In the past, our close proximity to workplace, shops and markets meant ease of physical access.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: There was no burning need to digitalise to bridge physical distances.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: However, the pandemic has made it necessary for organisations and companies to explore digital solutions, such as the use of Zoom, e-payment and e-commerce.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: We now better understand how digitalisation can help make our operations more convenient and efficient.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: The next step is to move from pockets of digitalisation or pilots to fully adopting real and sustainable digital transformation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: This will enable us to go beyond the superficial grafting of technology onto current processes and instead, leverage fully on digitalisation and create fundamental shifts to our business models.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How can MCI, MTI and MOM work closer together to support companies in driving real, sustained digital transformation?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: By stringing together cohesive programmes across Ministries to enable companies to build a coherent, successful transformation strategy and execution, possibly through a clear operation and technology roadmap from MTI, supported by skilled manpower through MCI's Digital Leaders Programme and SGUnited Jobs and Skills training guided by experienced practitioners using MCI CTO as a service while training organisational capabilities to drive insights from the better use of data.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Each Ministry holds a piece of the jigsaw puzzle.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Coming from the industry, trying to navigate transformation is difficult as this is not merely improving productivity but is fundamentally transforming business models.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Many companies may need help to navigate the multitude of different schemes available.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: To assist companies to fully leverage on the suite of support packages available, can the Ministry consider some form of overarching business transformation support through a membership programme or handholding to help companies navigate the cross-Ministerial support for transformation?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: We need a more concerted approach to business transformation to help companies gain traction and better navigate the diverse cross-Ministerial support provided.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: My second cut is about bridging the digital divide, in particular, inclusive growth for SMEs.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: One example of an SME that has performed well in their digital journey is Saffrons, an eatery in the east known for its fish briyani.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Through adopting digital tools such as food ordering, third party food delivery apps, digital posts, witty marketing and, of course, good food.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Its owner, Mr Rijal, shared that he has grown his customer base and revenue significantly.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Saffrons is an example of a small, non-digital native enterprise that has been able to leverage on digital transformation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Some SMEs are still struggling to find value through digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: With a lot of schemes available, how can MCI assist digital starters to navigate the eco-system of support?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How can MCI help businesses unlock new value through digitalisation, especially digital starters that need more assistance?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: With more home-based businesses (HBB) and Singaporeans in the gig economy, how can MCI also assist HBBs to unlock value?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: I applaud the continuous support for the SGUnited Jobs and Skills programme.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: I have met many residents who have benefited from the programme, from mid-career professionals to fresh graduates.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Of these, many hold aspirations for joining the growing ICT industry.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: However, some are still concerned that they lack the skills and industry background to seize digital opportunities.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Many share that despite taking up several digital courses, they have yet to be given an opportunity for a career in the industry.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: They cited that they have been turned down as they lack experience.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: But without the opportunity, they will never be able to switch industries and gain experience in the ICT industry.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How can MCI help workers get an opportunity in the industry and secure good jobs in the digital economy?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Can the Ministry consider some mechanism to balance the hiring of experienced and inexperienced talents in the growing ICT industry?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I therefore invite the Minister to share with this House the Ministry's plans to support and speed up the efforts of SMEs in the digital transformation of their businesses.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Mr Chairman, no fewer than 10 of our colleagues have spoken before me.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: For SMEs, it is important that initiatives deliver value quickly.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Otherwise, sign-up rates will be slow and dropout rates high.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: SME digitisation programmes often underperform because they do not meet the needs of the SMEs.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: As one SME told me, it is like these programmes only have one hammer and it does not matter what kind of nail I have.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: One way to bridge this is to focus on scalable use cases rather than broad topics or frameworks that they have to figure out how to apply themselves.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Getting value from any use case is also often about changing internal processes and driving a digital culture.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: It is therefore critical to provide a meaningful level of change management support.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: SMEs have quite different needs and expectations for the type of support and the degree of handholding.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Programme designs can therefore be more targeted and differentiated for different segments.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: In addition to this push approach of financing and grants, the Government can also work more with digital eco-system partners, especially tech giants, who are able to leverage their extensive networks and experience to pull support for SMEs.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: I also hope that the different Ministries involved in this space will ensure, for example, that digital traineeships and SME digitisation can be synced to leverage each other in order for us to maximise our investment value.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Otherwise, often, I find that MNCs are much more willing to accommodate digital trainees than our SMEs themselves.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: This will have to change for a sector that has to take 70% of our workforce.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Government had put in place the SMEs Go Digital and Hawkers Go Digital programmes to support their digitalisation efforts so as to transform their operations, increase productivity and expand their businesses.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With the COVID-19 pandemic hitting so many business sectors, what has been its impact on SMEs' adoption of digital technologies?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Digital transformation has not been uniform amongst the SMEs.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Which sectors are slower and how is the Government supporting them to overcome the difficulties that they face?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I took a browse at the IMDA website and found that there is indeed a long list of schemes and support with the very specific purpose to help SMEs.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: COVID-19 has given this unexpected boost to the adoption of digitalisation by businesses as well as consumers, who are using it more than before.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Can I seek an update on the progress so far?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: How far more do we have to go and what are the further support and assistance in store?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Mr Chairman, COVID-19 has heightened the importance of connectivity to enable people to continue to work, live and play.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Working from home arrangements, home-based learning and even communicating with family and friends would not have been possible without digital connectivity during this pandemic. 5G network technology can enable significantly enhanced connectivity and new capabilities.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: What is key about 5G is scale, low latency and high speed. 5G hence can transform and make possible connections previously not available, delivering new level of services, business models and experiences. 5G can make possible mission critical communication for infrastructure, emergency, security, medical and healthcare services.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: While the benefits of 5G are vast, implementation of 5G is complex and involves multiple stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
text: Increased connectivity and reliance on 5G networks will also increase cybersecurity risks.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Chairman, we have created a great start-up eco-system through innovative policies to attract many global firms to establish their headquarters in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With global tech giants like Google, Bytedance, Tencent, Microsoft, all having significant operations in Singapore, Singapore could become the Silicon Valley of Asia.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, Singapore could try to compete with Silicon Valley as the top place for start-up talent.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With the influx of billion-dollar companies providing stiffer competition, how is MCI continuing to develop and build the local eco-system for digital innovation to support home-grown start-ups?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, we still have a long way to go in finding that balance and calibrating between individual privacy and creating more connectivity and enhancing our quality of life.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With the digital landscape evolving rapidly, how are MCI and PDPC continuing to ensure that organisations respect privacy and are accountable for the data they handle?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In mid-December 2020, it was discovered that SolarWinds Orion's business software updates had been trajonised.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Due to SolarWinds' widespread global usage as a network management software, thousands of organisations, both private and public sector customers, were exposed to the malicious software update.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The SolarWinds cyberattack highlighted the danger of supply chain attacks and the abuse of authentication mechanisms to gain access to a victim's internal network.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To continually combat cybercrime and cyberattacks, how is MCI working to ensure that Singapore's critical information infrastructure and government systems, and user data, are secure and not exposed to backdoors for future attacks.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Mr Chairman, for many of us, much of our live reality now takes place online.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: This also means that highly-sensitive personal data is being shared readily, but also often unknowingly.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: For enterprises, cybersecurity is also becoming a day-to-day struggle, as cybercriminals, whose techniques are becoming increasingly sophisticated, continue with their attacks on different businesses.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: COVID-19 has forced businesses and companies to rely heavily on digital platforms to operate remote places.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: These platforms are, therefore, attractive targets and are extremely vulnerable to breaches if security is not adequately maintained.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Transformative 5G technology also makes us more connected than ever.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: How then will the Government better protect Singaporeans and enterprises in cyberspace?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Mr Chairman, there is a greater reliance on digital and tech across Government, businesses and individuals for connectivity, information access and exchange, and operations.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Vast amounts of sensitive and personal or commercial data are used and stored digitally.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: This increases the risk of cyberattacks, which could result in loss and unauthorised use of personal and sensitive data and disruptions to operations and activities.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: COVID-19 has driven the increased use of e-payments, mobile apps and e-wallets.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Smartphones are effectively becoming mobile financial transaction hubs.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: With higher volumes of e-commerce transactions, strengthening of supply chains is important as cyberattacks on supply chains are increasing.

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: Can the Minister share how are we strengthening Singapore’s cybersecurity?

speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
text: With the importance of cybersecurity, how are we growing our cybersecurity local talent base?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Data will be our most valuable resource and data connectivity infrastructure and enablers, both globally and in ASEAN, will be critical.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: There is a huge opportunity for Singapore to be both a thought leader and the trusted hub for secure, seamless cross-border data flows.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on its work, both globally and regionally on: number one, frameworks for data management including data categorisation and controls, as a common language for all parties in the digital economy; and, two, mechanisms for cross-border data flows to drive business innovation?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Chairman, on a related note, cyberspace has become a global common.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: Can the Ministry update on how Singapore is shaping the international governance of cyberspace, just as how we continue to shape international norms in the governance of air and sea spaces?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: The framework contributes to the global discourse on AI ethics by translating principles into practical recommendations for organisations to deploy AI responsibly.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
text: On this note, can the Ministry update on the framework and how it would continue to support our national AI strategy?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Can I ask how does the Government ensure that SingPost will continue to deliver good postal services and fulfil its obligations to serve the public well?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: How will the consumers' interests and the mail integrity and security be protected?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: The postal sector landscape has changed significantly in the recent years.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Can I seek the Minister's update on the current landscape and what is MCI's plan to transform the postal sector to meet changing consumers' needs?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Mr Chairman, I remember in my younger days exchanging letters with pen pals – yes, pen pals – pasting a stamp on the envelope and physically posting them.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Today, e-mails, e-invoices and many other electronic modes of communication have proliferated in the digital age, with letter mail in a steep decline.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: On the other hand, the advent of e-commerce has led to growing numbers of parcel and small packet deliveries.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: This has added a different logistical demand on our postal sector.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: We have seen this trend accelerate in 2020 given the COVID-19 restrictions in place.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I therefore invite the Minister to share with this House the Ministry’s plans to transform Singapore’s postal sector to meet changing consumer needs.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Mr Chairperson, Sir, it is truly commendable on the efforts of MCI and its officers in implementing Heartlands Go Digital and Hawkers Go Digital to help businesses transform digitally.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We note that the current efforts are laborious despite significance in results.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For smaller businesses, can MCI provide aggregated anonymised data on a regular basis so that SMEs can understand how data can help augment their businesses?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There is also a need to transform our postal sector to meet consumers’ needs such as e-commerce parcels.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Today, with digitalisation, consumers have a higher expectation towards faster and more convenient delivery of their parcels.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This form of non-contact delivery method reduces both economic and environmental cost due to reduction in door-to-door delivery.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: With a demand in e-commerce purchases, this creates a rise in reverse logistics due to consumers’ return of purchases.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Without a sustainable process, this can greatly counterbalance the efforts of parcel deliveries in reducing carbon footprint.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What efforts have MCI undertaken in this logistical challenge to ensure environmental sustainability?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: During key e-commerce seasonal sales, we observe higher volumes of packaging waste recycled at our blue bins.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, can MCI further integrate blue bins in our estates or can data on parcel delivery be shared with blue bin collection agency, so that removal frequencies can be calibrated accordingly to maximise yield and efficiency?

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, the growth of e-commerce has been accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: What is MCI doing to guide the postal sector towards a better regulated environment to ensure that consumers' interests are better protected?

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: How will MCI provide a guiding framework across public and private sectors for the provision of parcel locker infrastructure as well as service delivery standards to enable e-commerce to thrive and to enhance users' experience?

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: The prevalence of e-commerce is also challenging the viability of many traditional retail companies, who need to review their distribution model.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: How will the new regulated environment enable traditional retail companies to pivot seamlessly to an online business model?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: (In Mandarin):   Reading helps broaden our horizons and cultivate a broad range of interests.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Through reading, we can have better understanding on personal behaviour and gain more general knowledge.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: At a time when we are unable to travel abroad, reading allows us to better understand the history, culture and customs, as well as the latest developments of other parts of the world without going abroad.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: (In English): Many residents have shared with me that before the COVID-19 pandemic, the library was the place that they most like to frequent.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In the opening address at one of the reading events at Woodlands Regional Library 10 years ago, former Minister for Information, Communications and the Arts Dr Yaacob Ibrahim said, "Reading is essential to the development of our language and communication skills.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It deepens our knowledge and enriches our lives by opening us up to the new world and new experiences.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How are our libraries staying relevant in today's digital world?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And how will they continue to meet the needs of Singaporeans, in particular, families with young children and senior citizens?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mr Chairman, libraries are society’s portals to knowledge.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They play a central role in our younger generations’ journeys in learning, serve as a public space facilitating the transmission and exchange of ideas and culture, and they are also a great leveller as a provider of technology for the vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As Singapore and the rest of the world gets unceremoniously jolted into the digital future due to the pandemic, what can we do to ensure that our public libraries keep pace with technological advances?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can we ensure our libraries continue to serve Singapore residents by playing its social and curatorial roles?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In a world where a Google search often forms the first step of most, if not all quests in seeking knowledge, what are the evolutions our libraries need to make in order to ensure its continued relevance in the digital future?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And on a related note, how will the role of our librarians need to evolve so that they too, can keep pace with these inevitable changes?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mr Chairman, COVID-19 has forced the world to change the way we operate overnight.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The pandemic foisted upon us the digital future in double quick time.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Families increasingly reliant on e-commerce platforms for our everyday needs such as shopping for groceries.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Life events such as weddings and wakes conducted over video conferencing due to safe management measures.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Whatever the activity, the conclusion is one and the same: we have embraced digitalisation and there is no turning back, even when the pandemic finally ends.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And how do we ensure that our seniors are able to ride the fast and furious waves of new digital technologies?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How can we help our businesses to strike a sensible balance between maintaining existing legacy systems, yet at the same time, invest in digital business innovations?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And what is our digital strategy to support our SMEs and local large enterprises (LLEs) not only to remain buoyant, but coiled and ready to propel themselves to thrive in the digital global marketplace?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chairman, our youths are digital natives, born into a world where the internet is deeply integrated into our lives.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: From learning, entertainment, grabbing food, getting around, socialisation and civic discourse, digital tools have tremendous benefits and can be an equaliser.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We need to ensure that children from all walks of life are equipped to take advantage of the opportunities brought about by technology.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Still, the open nature of the digital realm presents dangers.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: From cyberbullying and exposure to unhealthy content to online radicalisation, the internet can also be polarising with social media warriors calling for people to blindly take sides instead of engaging in healthy discourse.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Seniors Go Digital was launched in May last year to help our seniors build digital capabilities.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: At the parliamentary debate last June, I stated my support for it, but was concerned about seniors who might not be able to make the digital leap.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The Minister clarified that the idea was to encourage the adoption of digital solutions, but to keep open the option of using non-digital solutions because there would be some who would still prefer them, or are uncomfortable with the digital part.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: To understand the impact of these schemes, could the Ministry clarify the following three aspects?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, what is the kind of reach that IMDA wants to achieve with the targeted 100,000 seniors?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Is the KPI geared at the numbers who attend the courses?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Or must a certain level of competency be demonstrated?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Second, what is the expected number to benefit from the Mobile Access for Seniors scheme?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And third, given the escalation of online scams, will the crime prevention aspects of the training be amplified?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Mr Chairman, MCI has made a good effort	to help seniors in this digital age.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The pilot project at	Geylang East Public Library one-stop access	to over 200 selected digital government services,	such as CPF nominations and CHAS applications is very useful.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Since the Seniors Go Digital programme was launched in 2020, how many seniors have been coached?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: How will IMDA scale up its digital literacy efforts to equip more seniors	with digital skills	to support	their everyday needs?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, COVID 19 has accelerated digitalisation in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: However, it also means that the vulnerable groups who were already disadvantaged before the pandemic may be left further behind.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: The Singapore Government has put in tremendous effort in trying to narrow the digital divide on the back of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Through the Home Access and NEU PC Plus programmes, many now have a digital device.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: However, increased digital device ownership would also mean that access to the support for maintenance would increase.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Low-income households may not be able to afford these services from existing shops.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng mentioned that non-profit organisations such as Engineering Good are already working with community partners to provide these services.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Ministry if we can tap on the networks and expertise of such organisations, who may already have ties with the Social Service Agencies, to help them expand their reach and enhance the suite of digital services they offer?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Digital literacy is also very important in this hyperconnected world.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Users need to be aware of issues such as cybersecurity risks and responsible online behaviours.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Practical skills like handling live- conferencing and dealing with internet connection issues would also need to be learnt.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Often though, the students from low-income households may have parents who are not digitally literate enough to support them in these matters.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: MOE already has a National Digital Literacy Programme for students.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Would MCI consider partnering MOE and/or other Social Service Agencies to offer the programme to parents as well?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I appreciate that IMDA will be streamlining the application for Public Rental Scheme households to ensure that they can auto-qualify for the assistance.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Beyond Social Services has a free wifi void deck project currently to counter that problem.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Would the Government consider working with similar organisations to roll this out to more rental households so as to not delay access to suitable internet connectivity?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Mr Chairman, we have seen how COVID-19 has accelerated digital innovation and transformed the way we live and work.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: We have seen many positive examples of our seniors carrying out essential tasks using digital means – SGQR codes for SafeEntry, e-payments just to name a few.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Many offer e-solutions and now are on-boarding e-commerce solutions and leveraging online marketplaces to sell their products and services.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: I am heartened by the efforts of our seniors and hawkers.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: And I note that there are still many Singaporeans who need more guidance and support to adapt to digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: We must not be complacent as there is a risk of widening the digital divide.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: MCI has done well to roll out digital inclusion initiatives like Hawkers Go Digital and Seniors Go Digital.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: I also note IMDA and National Library Board’s efforts to support low-income families and vulnerable groups via affordable internet access, and access to digital devices and eBooks.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
text: Hence, I would like to ask MCI to elaborate on its plans and partner stakeholders to drive ground up initiatives that will foster a digitally inclusive and ready society.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: In my main Budget debate speech, I had spoken on what we need to do to make digital basics available to the lower income – in terms of both hardware and broadband access.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: A third and important plank to this effort of digital access must be the digital savviness that is akin to street smartness in real life.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The dark corridors in the Digital Empire are as dangerous as those in real life – robberies are as common and lives can be ended as easily.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We need both trust and skepticism to survive as a social being.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: In our everyday life, we need to trust that the fishmonger at the market does not cheat us when he swears today’s catch is fresh, in the same way we rely on our social capital with our friends to keep their promises, and our business partners when they tell us their judgement on certain matters.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: During COVID-19, the importance of trusted and accessible information was felt acutely.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But truth online is a scarce commodity and as important as outside matters relating to the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How will MCI ensure that different groups with diverse needs can access trustworthy information?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How can we help build communities that will forge a collective sense of identity, so that we are all invested in keeping each other informed, each able to access and evaluate the quality of information in the digital world?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Beyond having the basic skills, individuals must also have the devices, networks and purpose to continuously immerse themselves in a digital environment.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How is MCI helping the vulnerable, or low-income families and youths gain the digital skills that they need?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Are we doing enough to prevent these less fortunate families from being left behind?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, the pandemic has made the internet a life tool to obtain full access to opportunities in a number of critical areas, including education, employment and health.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Many countries are grappling with a digital divide and Singapore is no exception.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What new policies will the Ministry introduce to narrow this divide and reduce the impact on future generations?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To better support our rental households, I cite the example of the ConnectHome initiative for low-income housing in the USA.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It offers affordable broadband access, technical training, digital literacy programmes and educational and workfare related content.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is a comprehensive programme to boost digital inclusion that goes beyond allowing residents to apply for devices and subsidies.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To help freelancers and employees working from home, can we explore some form of tax credit for individuals when they file their taxes or a tax break can also be extended to employers who pay for their employees' broadband access?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Before the pandemic, people could utilise broadband facilities in community spaces like libraries and schools.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I urge the Ministry to do more to ensure every household has access to quality digital connectivity within their homes.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: But we must not inadvertently create a new inequality or widen the existing gap, between those who can access and exploit the new digital technologies, and those who cannot.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: I am glad that this programme is beneficial and welcomed by seniors who felt dislocated by the accelerated pace of digitalisation.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Helping seniors embark and embrace digitalisation mitigates the sense of isolation brought about by a need for safe distancing measures so that our seniors can continue to lead more engaged, informed and fulfilling lives.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It is also heartening to see volunteer groups such as the Youth Corp helping seniors gain digital skills and corporates such as the ST Engineering donating to fund Mobile Access for Seniors and the NEU PC Plus for low-income students and persons with disabilities.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: Beyond equipping them with the devices, it is also important to help them use the digital tools effectively and wisely.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: What has been done and will be done to ensure that Government services and messages are delivered in a citizen-centric manner?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: So, we need to double down on our efforts to help everyone move ahead in our digitalisation journey.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: While we push ahead in our digital journey, it is also important that we leave no one behind and that we advance in one direction and as one people.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: There remains a group of seniors who cannot understand English and so, delivering messages in mother tongue is important.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It is of utmost importance that we intervene right now so that we do not allow this segment of Singaporeans become “Digital Outcast” eclipsed by the rapid pace of digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: In addition to the traditional offline channels, online and digital channels have seen increasing utilisation in Government communications and the share of use are expected to increase exponentially in the years to come.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: At the same time, our lives have also become complex and fast changing, requiring new approaches and more effective ways of reaching out to Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: We are also to be mindful of the diverse needs among us and, hence, the need to maintain multiple strategies.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Can I seek an update on the transformation of Government communications to groups with different needs?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Mr Chairman, the COVID-19 pandemic has led us to re-think the way we disseminate information, especially in Government communications.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: There is a need to ensure that all Singaporeans receive timely and accurate information that is relatable and capable of being understood by everyone with diverse needs.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: As we tap on digital means to communicate, how does the Government ensure that it does take into account different needs such as age groups, language barriers or level of digital literacy?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Conversely, it is important that the same digital channels are also accessible to receive valuable ground feedback on Government policies.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: The two-way channel between the Government and Singaporeans has always been the cornerstone of our policy making and needs to be preserved even as we transform our Government communications.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I, therefore, invite the Minister to share with this House the Ministry’s plans on the transformation of Government communications to reach all groups with diverse needs.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Chairman, last but not least, digital communications is expected to become the dominant mode of engagement amongst people, the Government and the private sector.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: With this widespread digital utilisation, the Government needs to find a range of methods to engage groups with diverse needs.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Would the Minister share what are the Ministry’s plans to ensure that it can reach as many Singaporeans and residents as possible on the various digital platforms?

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: How will it assist and reach vulnerable segments which may not have the digital skills and know-how, and access to the requisite software and hardware, such as Internet connection, devices and suitable software?

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: In addition to English, does the Government have plans to further augment its digital engagement with Singaporeans in the other three official languages – Malay, Chinese and Tamil – on all its platforms?

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In many ways, it has been a period of profound learning, adjustment and adaptation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Twenty-twenty saw years of digital transition occur in a matter of months.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And digital technologies can be a force for deep and lasting good.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Most of us have experienced this first-hand – families staying in touch with loved ones, students and teachers engaged in virtual lessons, employees working from home, businesses and customers transacting online.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But as noted by several Members, a larger digital footprint also means new and growing risks such as cyber attacks, data breaches, the rapid spread of misinformation and cyber bullying.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Against this backdrop, my Ministry strives to build a safe, inclusive and thriving digital future, where our citizens and businesses can fully reap the benefits of digital technologies while keeping the associated risks at bay.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The digital future we envision is underpinned by competitive enterprises that leverage digital technologies to innovate and grow; an inclusive society where every member can realise the benefits of globalisation and digitalisation; safe and secure digital spaces protected from malicious actors and online harms; robust digital infrastructure with fit-for-purpose regulations; and close collaboration with our community and enterprise partners.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As we respond to the various issues raised by Members, my colleagues Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary and I will elaborate on the work of the Ministry of Communications and Information to realise this vision.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Impelled by COVID-19, many traditional brick-and-mortar businesses have pivoted towards hybrid online-offline models to engage and transact with their consumers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Scent by SIX, a fragrance retailer at Bugis, took up an e-commerce solution under the SMEs Go Digital programme during the circuit breaker.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Its digital marketing efforts were so effective that revenues have increased by 25%, of which 60% were online.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The founder, Jason, is now exploring AR solutions that integrate social media with in-store shopping to create an omni-channel experience.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Don Wee asked about the progress of schemes to help enterprises transform digitally.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, the numbers are growing and we have to build on this progress so that more businesses and the workers they employ, can reap the benefits.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling, Ms Mariam Jaafar, Mr Eric Chua and Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked how the Government could aid businesses to to digitally transform and unlock economic value.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: MCI and IMDA will ramp up efforts to both broaden and deepen the digital reach among our SMEs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will support enterprises at every stage of growth, from start-up to scale up, to seize opportunities and realise the potential of emerging technologies and data.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For example, many SME leaders need help to devise a digitalisation plan to meet their needs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Therefore, IMDA will launch the Chief Technology Officer (CTO)-as-a-Service initiative later this year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The CTO-as-a-Service initiative will include a one-stop self-help web app for SMEs to assess their digital needs and gaps.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: SMEs can then access customised recommendations on digital solutions based on the company profile and information on Government support.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: SMEs that need more in-depth advice can tap on a shared pool of CTO-equivalents or Digital Consultants with expertise in areas such as data analytics, cyber security, and artificial intelligence.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They will receive both digital consultancy and project management services to not only identify needs and solutions, but also manage project implementation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, when Ms Mariam Jaafar talks about working with SMEs throughout the digitalisation journey, these are the kinds of measures we believe will help facilitate that.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I wanted to assure Mr Sharael Taha that all registered SMEs, including home-based businesses that are sole proprietorships, will be able to access these digital resources as well.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Beyond this broad-based approach, we also want to raise the peaks of our SMEs’ performance through a more holistic digital transformation of enterprises who are ready for that.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In this regard, the questions raised by Ms Tin Pei Ling on grooming the next wave of companies who can be digital leaders, and Mr Alex Yam on strengthening our competitive advantage globally are most pertinent.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It will also connect companies with tech partners to develop new digital products and services, and better position them to compete internationally.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The DLP will support up to 80 companies for a start, beginning with those more advanced in their digital journeys, with management teams that are committed to drive digital transformation for sustained growth.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The DLP will be managed by IMDA, in partnership with Enterprise Singapore and other economic agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To Ms Tin's question about support for local companies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: MCI will continue to study what more can be done to raise the competitiveness of local companies, including the several suggestions offered by Ms Tin.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As more businesses go digital, and more transactions go online, the volume and value of data will grow in tandem.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As noted by Ms Tin and Mr Edward Chia, data can yield valuable insights that improve business efficiencies and enhance products and services for consumers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As more data is collected, the risk of data breaches also increases.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: If data is not used responsibly, trust can be eroded, even undermined.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: On the one hand, we must accord due protection to personal data and privacy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: On the other, there is scope for businesses to use data responsibly for growth and innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This programme will provide businesses, particularly SMEs, with free tools and guidance to use their data responsibly to drive business growth.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The programme will also provide a free business intelligence tool that can convert raw data into visual dashboards that can aid business outcomes, such as, better sales and operational efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It will also enable more advanced data uses, such as for R&D and innovation, through curated resources, like case studies and videos.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We are also strengthening the accountability of businesses for the personal data they handle, a question raised by Mr Christopher de Souza.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The recently amended Personal Data Protection Act, has rules and a penalty framework to incentivise organisations to take proactive steps to minimise and manage data breaches.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But, going beyond that, the Personal Data Protection Commission Singapore, or PDPC, has issued guidelines that organisations can adopt to develop accountable governance practices.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The Data Protection Trust Mark also enables businesses to signal, and for consumers to discern, good data practices.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ultimately, we need to nurture a culture of good data governance – use and practice – and that has to come from not just regulations or penalties but also from education and industry efforts to share best practices.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ms Jessica Tan asked how we can ensure that consumers and businesses will benefit from 5G deployment.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The key is to build an ecosystem that supports the innovation and test-bedding of novel solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It is not just about providing the infrastructure, but it is in catalysing the collaboration between solution providers, service providers and end-users to come up with validated used cases.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: IMDA will facilitate such test-bedding through facilities such as PIXEL, the 5G Living Lab and initiatives such as the Open Innovation Platform.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 plan, or RIE2025.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: MCI will work with partner agencies to drive the co-creation and commercialisation of intellectual property, and enable capability transfer between research institutes and enterprises.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Translation will be a primary focus under RIE2025, and MCI will work with partner agencies to drive the co-creation and commercialisation of intellectual property, whilst enabling capability transfer between our research institutes and enterprises, to have that virtuous interaction between our public sector R&D effort with private sector value creation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This is how we are building up our local ecosystem for digital innovation, one of the points raised by Mr de Souza.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We want to go further in driving ground-up digital innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: IMDA's Open Innovation Platform, or OIP, was launched in 2018 to crowdsource and match the demand from business challenges to a supply of innovative solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: It has grown into a vibrant eco-system with over 10,000 registered users.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This will help more enterprises access innovative solutions, and accelerate the deployment of digital innovation at scale.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: IMDA will also co-fund the prototyping of matched challenges to help innovative tech companies expand their market base.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Chairman, even as we pursue these exciting opportunities, we must pay heed to the very real concerns of mature workers and seniors, and also our youth and fresh graduates, over the accelerated pace of digitalisation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They worry if they will have a place in this digital future, especially if they do not have backgrounds in tech, or an inclination for engineering and software development.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Sharael Taha raised a similar point asking how we can further support mature workers or those who have no ICT background enter the tech sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I met Nurul Baizura, a part-time undergraduate, who was selected to participate in Google's Skills Ignition SG programme.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: She previously worked at a data storage company, handing network infrastructure and patching.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Today, she is learning skills in an entirely new area – cloud technology – and she is passionate about her role as cloud engineer.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ganapathi, whom I met recently, is a mid-career project manager who was previously from the education sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Though he lacked the technical expertise, Gana joined the programme with NCS – one of our tech company partners – in 2020, and is well on his way to becoming an applications consultant.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will continue to expand our TeSA programmes, to develop more local talent in areas such as digital marketing, as well as for more tech-intensive roles in product and software development.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: These programmes will provide a wide spectrum of Singaporeans like Nurul and Gana, with more opportunities to develop their careers in such roles across the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Several Members have emphasised the importance of attracting talent to this talent-starved sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As we invest in the development of our local pipeline of talent, nurturing the tech leaders for the future, we also have to ensure that we are able to attract quality talent from around the world to come in and have a judicious complement of them to support our overall effort.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And this is how we would ensure that we sustain our position as a digital innovation hub.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In that regard, it is not just MCI but across the economic agencies and beyond, we are undertaking a whole-of-Government effort to attract Singaporean talent that is based overseas and other talent so that they can come in, working with our local companies, our large and mid-sized players in order to contribute to the evolution of the digital eco-system in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Tin Pei Ling have emphasised that employers must leverage the talent pool of women in STEM.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: MCI aims to grow the ICT talent pipeline and this includes attracting more women to join the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In collaboration with community and industry partners, IMDA launched the SG Women in Tech initiative in 2019 to encourage more women to explore careers in tech.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: There has been good momentum with the movement reaching more than 117,000 through activities and events such as SG100 Women in Tech.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: In 2017, 28% of the intake to Information Technology courses in our local Universities were female.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: I think the message is getting through and certainly we need to enlist the help of some of our women tech leaders including the likes of Ms Jessica Tan and Ms Janet Ang and many others in this House and without, to get this message out and encourage more women to consider a career in tech.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: More broadly, we want all Singaporeans to be able to participate meaningfully and safely in online engagements.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The volume and value of transactions has grown four-fold, from June 2020 to today.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui and Ms Sylvia Lim enquired about the impact of the Seniors Go Digital programme.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: But, I want to emphasise and in response to Ms Sylvia Lim's point, it is not just about numbers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Numbers are important because we do want scale.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We want to imbue our seniors with the confidence and the comfort to navigate technology and use it to derive benefits that will enhance their lives.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As the Member and others would appreciate, this is not an easy task, but one that we are fully committed to and it is a journey with rich rewards, but we have to make the effort.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We would welcome any suggestions that the Member or others may have, to further strengthen the message and its impact on our community of seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Senior Minister of State, Sim Ann will elaborate further on the work done by ESG, IMDA and other Government agencies, with respect to the work we are doing in the heartlands.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our seniors, hawkers and heartland shops are excellent role models.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: They demonstrate that young or old, big or small, whatever our background, with the right mindset and can-do spirit, we can all make the digital transition.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our libraries play a critical role in nurturing that spirit of exploration and learning among all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ms Hany Soh and Mr Eric Chua asked how our libraries are staying relevant in a world that is digital.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For some time now, but especially in the past year, NLB has expanded its digital resources and collections, introduced digital storytelling for children and conducted online programmes for all ages, including seniors.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: NLB produced learning packages on subjects like pandemics, provided home access to digital newspapers and conducted a series of webinars on topics ranging from cybersecurity to health and wellness.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For the longer term, NLB will continue to explore new ways to provide reading and lifelong learning opportunities for all Singaporeans, and nurture an informed citizenry.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Informed by public feedback and its own experience, NLB has developed the Libraries and Archives Blueprint 2021-2025 to reimagine the service models of libraries and archives of the future.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: What we have today is a precious resource that has adapted and innovated in response to consumer needs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: And now, we are thinking ahead to the next phase and how our libraries can continue to evolve with the needs and the times.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will provide more details.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Like NLB, as more engagement shift to the digital space, individuals and businesses will be exposed to more risks and online harms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: So, it is incumbent that our digital spaces are kept safe and secure, with members of online communities protected from malicious actors and other harms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Alex Yam have asked how we are safeguarding our critical systems against sophisticated threats and disruptions to operations.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The security of our digital systems is critical because they are the very foundation of our digital economy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Hence, we will do our utmost to lay a strong digital foundation – a communications infrastructure that is secure and resilient and legislation that is robust and fit-for-purpose.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will also continue to safeguard our digital space to protect our people from the harms inflicted by malicious threat actors.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Such incidents serve to remind us that cyber threats are real, trans-border and constantly evolving.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To derive the benefits of digitalisation, we must be ever vigilant against cyber risks and we need continuous and sustained efforts to strength our cyber security posture.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Senior Minister of State Janil will elaborate further.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: To build trust in online spaces, we must also ensure safeguards against harmful online content that may harm individuals and divide society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our regulation and public education efforts have helped Singaporeans deal with potential dangers online, such as misinformation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: MCI and MHA are therefore studying how to enhance our regulations to deal with serious online harms and their real-world effects on society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We will share our findings and recommendations in due course.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Ultimately, the first line of defence in our fight against misinformation is a well-informed citizenry who receive accurate communications from reliable sources in a timely manner.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Don Wee have asked how the Ministry is ensuring that groups with different needs can access reliable information.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This has been our foremost communications challenge in battling COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our focus was to broaden and deepen the reach of Government communications by leveraging both traditional and newer digital platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: This was to ensure that all segments of our population were informed of key developments of the pandemic, why certain measures were necessary and how they could play their part to protect the health and safety of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: The mainstream media played an important role in this national effort.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We also worked with the People's Association and Silver Generation Office for face-to-face outreach to those who may not have access to or use digital media.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Polls conducted by REACH indicate that more than eight in 10 are satisfied with the information provided by the Government on COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: For the next phase of our fight against the pandemic, we have launched the VacciNationSG campaign to raise awareness of the vaccination programme, address misconceptions, debunk misinformation and mobilise action.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will elaborate more on our efforts, including the use of multiple languages and channels to make information accessible to all segments of our society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Partnership – with industry, the community and fellow Singaporeans – has been the anchor of our efforts to overcome the challenges posed by the pandemic but also to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
