text: Industry partners have stepped up with initiatives to re-structure our economy and create new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Our community partners and citizens also organised themselves to support fellow Singaporeans in need.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Engineering Good, a non-profit organisation, collected laptops from the community to help less privileged students access home-based learning resources during the circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As we venture into the digital future, such partnerships with our stakeholders will be even more important to ensure that new and more complex challenges do not deter us from fully seizing digital opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah and Mr Shawn Huang asked how we can partner with stakeholders to drive ground-up initiatives to foster a digitally inclusive society.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Such sentiments were also expressed during the Emerging Stronger Conversations, where the impact of digitalisation and how we can harness technology for better social outcomes was one of the most discussed topics.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Through this national movement, we want to encourage and support ground-up efforts to co-create solutions that enable all Singaporeans to benefit from digital technology.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: We invite all who wish to make a difference to the digital growth and wellness of fellow Singaporeans to join us in this journey.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Senior Minister of State Sim Ann will elaborate further.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to conclude by emphasising the Government's resolute commitment to build a safe, inclusive and thriving digital future for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
text: As we work in partnership with our community and business stakeholders, I have every confidence that we are well placed to build a shared digital future with a place for every Singaporean.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the various Members for their cuts and questions and I hope to address several of them in my response, especially those from Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Alex Yam, Mr Seah Kian Peng, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Mr Christopher de Souza.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The digital space has had a deep impact on our daily lives and this transformative effect will continue for some time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For many Singaporeans, digitalisation carries the promise of more convenience, more efficiency and more options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we do more online, we face an increased risk of cyberattacks, online scams and data breaches.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need the online environment to be an enabler so that our people can benefit from the opportunities of this digital age.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, I will focus on how we develop online safety and security – the strong foundations of our plans for digitalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our strategies have to cover a broad range from infrastructure development, regulations and partnerships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need to address a wide variety of issues so that our companies and our people can trust the digital systems that are so central to our lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Beyond assurance, we want people to step up, to be empowered, to take charge of their online safety and to embrace the digital age with confidence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Strong foundations depend on a robust digital infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our past investments in this infrastructure have recently enabled workers to switch to telecommuting and students to attend online lessons with relative ease during the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, robust digital infrastructure alone cannot guarantee safe and secure spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Other keys to a strong foundation are a robust regulatory regime and an approach to remain relevant and fit-for-purpose amidst the evolving technological landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Data is a critical resource used to inform business decisions and also power emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Personal data requires strong safeguards and accountability but there is a balance we need to strike.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: You overcorrect for business innovation and you undermine consumer protection, privacy and trust.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: On the other hand, pursuing consumer interests narrowly hampers, potentially, business development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The public may ultimately suffer from poorer and more costly services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our strong foundations therefore also need us to be agile and calibrated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We recently amended the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, you may subscribe, to the mailing list of an online shop and as a result, you can receive customised recommendations based on your browsing history or based on your prior transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is a benefit to you as a customer, as the consumer, from having shared your data.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Under the amended PDPA, if there is a data breach which may cause significant harm to affected individuals, you are to be notified directly by the shop so you can take timely, proactive measures to protect your data, such as by changing your passwords.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If you choose to opt out of the mailing list, the shop is required to remove your details from the list and stop sending you recommendations within a reasonable period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, businesses, as a result of the amendment, are held to a higher standard with more transparent and accountable practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Like data, electronic transactions are also central to the global economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To support wider digitalisation, the Parliament passed the amendment to the Electronic Transactions Act this year to adopt the Model Law on Electronic Transferable Records from the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The shipping, logistics and finance sectors now stand to benefit from faster and more secure electronic transactions compared to paper-based transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We expect to see benefits in terms of efficiency, productivity and, hopefully, cost savings as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One concern arising from our digital push is the rise in online scams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We take this matter very seriously – it is something that people are anxious about, it erodes trust in their transactions and their activities online – and we are working across the Government to tackle these scams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, we require telcos to attach the "+" symbol for all incoming overseas calls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: IMDA also requires telcos to enhance capabilities to block calls from commonly spoofed numbers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, the space is dynamic, there is an evolving behaviour of scammers and people who try to do malice to us, so existing solutions to block scam calls from overseas will never be foolproof.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, no telco can verify with absolute certainty that a given incoming call is fraudulent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, IMDA is working with the telcos to build new analytic capabilities within their networks to better identify and block spoofed calls with numbers that appear local, without blocking legitimate calls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These measures fit in with what MHA is doing in terms of their broader approach to mitigate scams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to work closely with MHA through the Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Cybersecurity threats are also growing in both number and sophistication.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Members have just heard about the recent SolarWinds breach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This cyberattack compromised a network management software used extensively by major companies and governments worldwide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Notably, the software that was compromised was trusted and had privileged access to internal networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It was a very sophisticated attack that went undetected for months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Singaporeans are concerned about whether our systems are safe; so are we.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And sensitive information needs to be sufficiently protected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With more activities taking place online, it is important that people trust the digital systems we use to store, collect and transfer our information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The reality is that we will not be able to prevent every cyberattack – malicious actors only need to exploit one vulnerability to compromise our systems, while defenders must safeguard systems under their charge against all threats, all the time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Consistent and deliberate efforts to strengthen our cybersecurity are thus critical.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Many essential services like banking and healthcare are powered by information and communications technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These systems are our Critical Information Infrastructure or CIIs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, all CII owners must maintain a mandatory level of cybersecurity as part of the Cybersecurity Act.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, we also recognise that most organisations, including CII owners, engage vendors to support their operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Therefore, we also need to manage cybersecurity risks across the supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Doing so requires CII owners to have a better understanding of their vendors to identify systemic risks and improve the level of cyber hygiene with the vendors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The programme will provide recommended processes and sound practices for all stakeholders to manage cybersecurity risks in the supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The discussions that we will have with the stakeholders as a result of this programme will also help the Government improve our policies around supply chain security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the longer term, our CII sectors and the companies there will also need to adopt a zero-trust cybersecurity posture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This shift in mindset is necessary to defend against supply chain attacks by highly sophisticated threat actors, such as those behind the SolarWinds breach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In concrete terms, this means that CII owners should not trust digital activity in their networks without verification.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They should also authenticate continuously, detect anomalies in a timely manner, and validate transactions across network segments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This work will continue and will become increasingly complex in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Cybersecurity therefore has to be a collective effort and a core part of our lives in this digital age – integrated into the products we use and the way we behave online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As more enterprises go digital, our exposure to cyber threats grows in parallel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, we will provide informational resources and educational material for key roles including C-suite executives, cybersecurity teams and frontline employees, based on their specific roles and knowledge needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need to shift attitudes and raise cybersecurity awareness through in-house training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This means that if you are a consumer, a business looking for an HR processing service for example, and care about the cybersecurity level of the service provider, you may look for this Trustmark for added assurance that this service provider takes cybersecurity seriously.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our cybersecurity talent base is a key enabler of these efforts and we are working closely with industry partners and Government agencies to nurture and grow our cybersecurity workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, to meet near-term demand, we facilitate the training and upskilling of cybersecurity professionals, as well as fresh and mid-career non-cybersecurity professionals for cybersecurity jobs, through programmes such as IMDA’s Tech Skills Accelerator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: All of us need to play our part to create a safer and more secure cyberspace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are things that we can do as individuals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We should enable two-factor authentication, update our software in a timely manner, choose a passphrase rather than a password, and stay vigilant to spot the signs of phishing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But there are also things that we do as a country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Singapore participates actively in international discussions to develop and implement norms in line with our interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For instance, we are producing an implementation checklist with specific actions that countries can take to implement cyber norms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This effort contributes to a rules-based multilateral order in cyberspace, and gives all states, big or small, confidence, predictability and stability, essential for economic progress, job creation and technology adoption.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It translates key ethical AI principles such as human centricity into practical measures, in line with our National AI Strategy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ultimately, we lay strong foundations so that our people can look ahead, and reap the full benefits of the digital economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will remain open and integrated with the global economy to enable our companies to maximise opportunities beyond our shores.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These DEAs facilitate seamless end-to-end digital trade, enable trusted data flows and build trust in digital systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Beyond these DEAs, businesses can look forward to further support for transferring data to and from overseas seamlessly and securely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With these ready-to-use and flexible templates to transfer personal data, businesses operating in ASEAN markets stand to benefit from shorter contract negotiations on data flows.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These will only grow as technologies evolve and become more complex.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Trust in our digital systems is key to the success of our digital economy efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And without the trust to transact, or to innovate, our best efforts to develop our digital ecosystem and reap the dividends, create opportunities, will fall short.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Strong foundations such as I have described will fortify our defences against online threats, and support this trust that we need to grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need our companies and people to be aware of the risks, vigilant of the manifestations of these risks, and make informed choices to protect our safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We can and must make the online space more secure and more trusted and thus create more opportunities for all of us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Chairman, the past year has been challenging, to say the least, and we have all come to value the importance of staying connected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Digitalisation has been critical in enabling us to do so, even as we adopt safe distancing measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are transforming digitally as a society, but we need to ensure that the transformation is inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will elaborate on four key strategies to achieve this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, we know not all Singaporeans are progressing at the same pace in the digital journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Regardless of your starting point, the Government and key stakeholders will support you with the necessary resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, we will forge strong partnerships with stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, we will continue to improve our last-mile delivery infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Minister of State Low Yen Ling and I co-chair the Heartland Digitalisation and Revitalisation Committee, and she has earlier spoken on how the Committee is helping heartland enterprises to keep pace with digitalisation, taking into account their unique context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Under the Hawkers Go Digital initiative, we have been acting on stallholders’ feedback to make improvements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, IMDA and the SG Digital Office are working with NETS to enhance the NETSBiz mobile app, with features such as a bigger font size, the use of colour and a distinct audio alert, to make it easier for busy stallholders to track their payment transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Eric Chua, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Seah Kian Peng and Dr Shahira Abdullah asked about the efforts made to ensure that low-income families do not lag behind in the digital future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Singapore is a highly connected society, where 98% of all households have access to broadband and own Internet-enabled devices such as computers or smartphones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We recognise low-income households and vulnerable groups may require more help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: A central thrust of MCI’s work is helping them access digital tools and remain connected with the larger society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This includes a second subsidised laptop for larger families with school-going children during COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have streamlined the application process for households supported by ComCare, to make it easier for them to get onto the programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: IMDA is working to automatically include recipients of HDB’s Public Rental Scheme for the Home Access programme in the coming months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is a growing sense that many in the community would like to contribute and support fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I chaired an Emerging Stronger Conversation on Digital Readiness in November last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The 60 participants had a robust discussion on digital adoption challenges faced by vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The movement will support community activities that promote digital technology and inclusion, as well as digital literacy and wellness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It will be a platform where like-minded individuals from corporates, community and Government agencies, can utilise their skills, experience and know-how in helping those who need a little extra assistance, and in building inclusive, safe and secure digital spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government will empower and support them to catalyse meaningful changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: One project I feel strongly about is protecting women and youth from online harms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As a Member of Parliament, I have encountered calls for help from distressed women and their loved ones, because their intimate pictures have found their way online without their consent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I have also heard disturbing stories about how our youths are being harassed and received unsolicited lewd pictures, with some coming to view this as “normal”.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin has raised the same concern about protecting our youths, especially young girls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I met some community partners last week to discuss how we can tackle such online harms and mitigate the real-world damage they cause.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These partners have shown strong interest to create more impactful public education and resource support for potential victims, and in offering policy ideas to shape a safer cyberspace for women and girls and, indeed, for men and boys, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These can complement other measures, such as the Better Internet Campaign by the Media Literacy Council, MCCY’s work on promoting youth cyberwellness, and MOE’s work in the schools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: With the Digital for Life Movement, I hope that the community can be empowered to hold conversations and collaborate even on thorny and complex social issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To help Singaporeans pick up digital skills, our much-loved libraries have been transforming themselves into digital learning hubs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As mentioned by Minister, NLB will be embarking on the Libraries and Archives Blueprint 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Going forward, our libraries will feature digital services that enhance experiential learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The revamped Choa Chu Kang Public Library, set to reopen later this year, will feature digital services which encourage appreciation of natural landscapes and biodiversity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Augmented Reality elements will allow library users to interact with selected books through their mobile devices, making content come alive, almost literally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last week, I visited the Tampines Regional Library and chatted with seniors who learnt how to use the libraries' services, such as e-newspapers and the NLB mobile app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They appreciated the human touch of having our Digital Ambassadors walk them through the steps, and having someone to turn to whenever they need a refresher.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the library's makerspace, library users of various age groups were enjoying the use of technology, such as robotics and 3D printing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: There is truly something for everyone in NLB's growing suite of digital offerings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The role of librarians, as alluded to by Mr Eric Chua, will evolve in the digital future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Librarians will need to put together inter-disciplinary knowledge, taking into account societal trends, and how people learn and acquire information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NLB cannot do this alone and will collaborate with volunteers and partners with diverse interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We agree with Mr Don Wee and Ms Hany Soh that every Singaporean should have access to NLB resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is why NLB brings library books to reading corners at partner spaces, such as community centres and Family Service Centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For many years, NLB has been supporting the Singapore Prison Service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: NLB will continue to develop ways to support under-reached communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Mr Cheng Hsing Yao asked about MCI’s plans to transform the postal sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is addressed by our third strategy – which is to continue investing in digital infrastructure, so as to make the benefits of the digital economy more accessible to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: E-commerce has become an important part of our lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last year, I shared that we would be rolling out a nationwide parcel locker network, to give convenience to Singaporeans and enhance productivity for merchants and logistics service providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: IMDA and its subsidiary Pick have been trialling these parcel lockers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The feedback received from close to 10,000 residents has been overwhelmingly positive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Ng Kum Yin, a 71-year-old retiree, looks forward to the locker stations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Mr Ng and his wife shop online for consumer electronics and health supplements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: He is concerned by news of missing parcels left outside homes, so he is keen to try out the parcel lockers whenever they are ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are targeting nationwide deployment by the end of 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To address the growth in e-commerce and benefit both consumers and industry, we are reviewing the Postal Services Act this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More details will be shared at a later date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On postal delivery, since December last year, SingPost has been trialling PostPal, a smart letterbox system, at Clementi, serving about 200 households in total.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Residents like the convenience of using the app to find out if there is any mail for them to retrieve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: SingPost has seen an increase in productivity of 75% for their postmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ninety-four percent of the mail can go through the auto-sorting feature in the smart letter box, which means greater accuracy in mail delivery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These innovations are part and parcel of our collective effort to seek efficiency improvements and better value for consumers and residents, while making good use of technology and digitalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The fourth strategy is to strengthen our Government communication efforts, making information accessible to all citizens with diverse backgrounds and language needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Despite COVID-19, REACH connected with more than 59,000 Singaporeans last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To engage safely, REACH opened up new channels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These include online Listening Points and online dialogues, such as the Emerging Stronger Conversations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: During the Circuit Breaker, the REACH WhatsApp chat group discussions were maintained 24/7.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have established diverse platforms to reach out to our audiences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, gov.sg has now gone into the heartlands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Some 14,000 Digital Display Panels are found within HDB lifts and at lift landings, making important Government information accessible to Singaporeans at their doorstep.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are pushing out content in the four official languages wherever possible, across platforms like free-to-air television, radio, newspapers and WhatsApp messages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On Ms Tin Pei Ling’s question, to reach out to members of the Chinese community who are seniors and who communicate primarily in dialects, key Government messages are weaved into programmes that run on Mediacorp’s dialect belt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have also worked with Mediacorp to introduce sign language interpretation for key national events, such as the Prime Minister’s COVID-19 addresses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is on top of the longstanding practice of subtitling or closed captioning, wherever possible, for Government communications on free-to-air television and Government’s social media channels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Accurate and contextualised translation is important for effective Government communications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Last year, MCI rolled out two new translation initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Malay and Tamil-speaking volunteers have told us that they are keen to help with the standardisation of translated terms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Chinese-speaking volunteers are interested in post-editing and vetting machine-generated translations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We look forward to working with our Citizen Translators to improve Government translations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Public officers can now generate machine translations in all four official languages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The SG Translate web portal – called SG Translate Together – will be progressively opened to members of the public this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Seniors Go Digital website and the TraceTogether mobile app are already available in our four official languages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government is committed to translating more Government digital services, where necessary, so that those who are more comfortable with their mother tongues can access Government digital services with greater ease.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But some Singaporeans are still hesitant and uneasy about using digital technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To ensure that all Singaporeans embrace digitalisation with ease and confidence, we will continue to rollout and expand initiatives to help Singaporeans grasp digitisation tools and skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These programmes aim to help participating companies integrate digital technologies into their business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That way, companies can also compete on the international stage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the individual level, the Government has set up in-person touchpoints at libraries and in community centres where Digital Ambassadors help less digitally savvy Singaporeans pick up digital skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have taken care to include the human touch in these public education efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For Singapore to succeed in digitalisation, we will need to work with Singaporeans, the community and companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Through the Digital For Life Movement, we will work with our partners to champion causes they are passionate about and to leverage on their expertise so that they will be able to help vulnerable Singaporeans enjoy benefits of digitalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government continues to prioritise the quality of translation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We have launched the Citizen Translators initiative where we reach out to volunteers to co-create solutions for the most suitable translations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We are encouraged by the public's response to this initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We look forward to work them to improve Government translations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The digital future presents many opportunities for different segments of our citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government will continue to work with partners from the people and private sectors to strengthen the digital eco-system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This way, Government-led programmes and community initiatives can complement each other and create greater value for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We look forward to forging an inclusive and digital Singapore together.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Chairman, I thank the Member for his clarification.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think when the Member uses the term "Silicon Valley of Asia", it is really a kind of a shorthand to describe what is essentially a confluence of opportunity, an enabling environment and talent.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think, in that regard, even before COVID-19, we already had a certain momentum to bring that confluence about in order to create a thriving opportunity within the tech eco-system in Singapore and, through Singapore, into Asia.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And to answer the Member's specific question, I think COVID-19 has, if anything, given this further impetus.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: First, obviously in catalysing digital innovation in order to deal with the challenges that COVID-19 has thrown up but, in the process, also triggering a larger scale of adoption of digital technologies and, in a sense, a desire for more digital solutions because the value proposition has been internalised and now there is a desire to adopt and scale.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In fact, the Member himself mentioned this in his speech and several others have alluded to this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But we have also seen many of the mid-sized, and even our local enterprises, moving in that direction.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: The third point I would make is, because it is about confluence with talent, and this is where we have been making significant efforts – as I had explained and my colleagues also elaborated – both in terms of developing our local base, which is important, investing not just in the pipeline that is upstream from our Universities and pre-employment training and education, but also in endowing our workforce, those especially in their mid-careers, with the requisite skills to make that pivot into tech.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But at the same time, we are also engaged to attract talent that can complement our local base judiciously.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is something we are purposefully going about in partnership with other economic agencies, and that includes those under MTI.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And it is about attracting Singaporeans who are based overseas, who would want to come back, perhaps, and we have seen many like that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But also other talent from other nationalities, who can judiciously complement our capabilities.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, in sum, Mr Chairman, to answer the Member's question, there is certainly an opportunity for us to build on this.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Whether I would use the moniker "Silicon Valley of Asia", well, I would apply that with some restraint.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But, I think, certainly, we have the opportunity to be a thriving, secured, vibrant digital hub in this part of the world and part of the global eco-system.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: Chairman, I am heartened to understand from Senior Minister of State Sim Ann that the new Choa Chu Kang library will have very good offerings.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: So, when the library is undergoing renovation now, there is a book dispenser, which is placed at Lot One, Level 1 currently.

speaker: Mr Don Wee
text: So, I wonder if NLB can consider shifting the book dispenser to the nearest rental block, which houses about 500 units of young families, once the renovation is over, and since the rental block is only about 2 km away from Lot One?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: It was placed indeed to help meet the gap, while our renovations are on-going.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will take his suggestion back and study and get back to him.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Sounds like a very good programme as we need to grow our digital leaders.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Will it be by industry or the value proposition that they are looking for?

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member for his question.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because if I go back to the point I made at the start, this is about not just broad-based scale in terms of the digitalisation reach, it is also about peaks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In other words, we are now trying to empower companies that are ready and able, to move forward, adopting more advanced digital technologies, with the capabilities and, critically, the talent that will enable them to maximise.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is more a function of the readiness and willingness of these companies to adopt the technology and to really be able to leverage it for the next bound of their digital growth.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: I would really like to thank the Senior Minister of State for addressing my point earlier on.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: I was very keen and heartened to know that there have been discussions on how we can protect our women and girls online.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: And this is particularly poignant as this is the year of celebrating Singapore Women.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: I know it is preliminary but could the Senior Minister of State please share some of the ideas raised during the discussion and the type of partners who are involved?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: I have heard parents shared how they feel really ill-equipped to deal with, for example, Tik Tok, Snapchat and OnlyFans.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: But we know that banning and deleting these apps will not solve the issue.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: So, I hope that any efforts, moving forward, will involve equipping parents as well.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is especially of concern if youngsters, including young girls, are targeted.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: For this cluster of issues, there is the aspect of looking at whether or not our existing laws are applicable, and to ensure that reporting mechanisms are timely and effective.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Very often, these are of women and girls, but we do not rule out men being the victims as well.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This would fall under, very broadly, the ambit of harassment.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is something which on-going discussions, not just within the MCI family but also within the MHA family, about online harms and how to strengthen them, and how to also work with platforms to mitigate these harms would be very pertinent.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, for instance, users of social media platforms receiving unsolicited lewd pictures or very suggestive questions.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: And very often, not quite knowing how to react to these unwanted advances.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: For many of the social media platforms, community standards do exist but it is a question of whether users are fully aware of what these standards are and what they must do in order to protect themselves.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: So, for instance, we hear that a very common reaction of people who receive such unwanted advances is to delete them.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: But once it is deleted, the proof is gone, and that is something that quite a lot of public education and support would be helpful to protect the next woman or girl or, indeed, man or boy, from becoming the next victim.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: I particularly want to express my deep appreciation as it is very evident that the approach that has been taken is a very inclusive one, with the focus on SMEs, hawkers and the elderly and also vulnerable women.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: I am very glad to hear of the move to different kinds of schemes, so including more customisation and deeper hand-holding for digital starters.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: For example, the CTO-as-a-Service as well as for our Digital Leaders Programme.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Ideally, I hope that this will also be somewhat sector-specific, and also address – as I had said in my cut – the internal process and the change management that would need to go along with any advice on adoption of digital solutions.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: At the same time, I do want to raise a little caution, having heard some feedback on earlier programmes, which is that SMEs themselves tend to under-estimate the degree of hand-holding needed, and how hard it is, actually, to make a digital transformation.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Perhaps, at this point, I should probably declare my interest as a consultant in this space.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: Because I really do think that it is important for SMEs to get onboard.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
text: So, if it comes to a matter of looking at ways, for example, to fund the journey, let us not skimp on the cost but actually think forward and proactively about how we can enable the highest number of SMEs.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Mr Chairman, I think the Member has made an important point, which is really that when we embark on an effort like this, which is, in essence, a kind of customisation at a mass scale, mass customisation, as she puts it, the challenges are considerable and we should not under-estimate the effort that is required.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: We are talking about a very large base of enterprises.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And they vary significantly in size, scale and complexity, from the MSMEs all the way to the mid-sized players; and also those larger than that.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And that is also evidenced in the way we have structured our programmes.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, if you look at the SMEs Go Digital, it has a got a suite of possibilities, offerings from payment solutions to going online for marketing and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And all of these are enterprises that are already at a certain scale and wanting to make this adaptation.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: But we have also got the Start Digital programme which is really about those who are starting up their business but they can already adopt some of the digital solutions.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And then we have the other extreme, the scaling up programmes, where they can go international by using some of these.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And as I emphasised, it is also to work with the SMEs on the execution of that plan.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because it is not just about a set of tools and then putting them into the system.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: As we all know, it is about the integration and then, how you adapt to your work processes to that new set of tools.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think that is key to realise the full benefits.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, that is our intention around the CTO-as-a-Service idea.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Hence, the numbers are smaller; I think this point that was raised.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: Because we need to train our sights on those that can do this, that are ready for it because they already journeyed somewhat.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: In summary, I would say it is different strokes for different folks.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And we have to find that spectrum of capabilities, both in the toolkit that we have in Government but also, as the Member put it, ultimately the customer must also understand what it entails.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is not just about making a decision, "Let's go digital".

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: It is also about understanding what it entails and the kind of commitment that is required in terms of the technology you bring into the organisation but, most importantly, how you invest in your people and your systems to take full advantage of it on a sustainable basis.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Can I also remind Members to keep their clarifications short?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: My short clarification is in relation to the digitalisation of libraries, my request is that we do not overdo this.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Because there is something about flipping through a hardcopy book, bringing your family and your children and introducing them to the library where you go and pick a book according to the author, and return the book according to the author, keeping quiet, it is a communal space; and reading a book that has been read before and the pages have been touched before.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I think that is something very intimate and special.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: That is something unique to the reader and unique to hardcopy books.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, in as much as we try to digitalise the reading of books, can we do this in a very calibrated fashion so that we pass on to the next generation the love for holding a hardcopy book and taking in the story physically as it were.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: As long as we disinfect the book, yes.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I am sure there is a shorter answer.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I thought I should respond to this clarification, with the indulgence of my colleague Minister of State Sim Ann.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: I think many of us share the Member's appreciation of the tactile experience of reading a physical book and also of gathering physically in the library and so on.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: And in turn what you experience in the library can then be carried on virtually through digital platforms.

speaker: Mr S Iswaran
text: So, really, what we envisage is a virtuous cycle between the physical and the virtual, and we want to ensure that we are able to keep the finest traditions of our libraries very much alive and thriving even as we go down the path of digitalisation.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Tin, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: It has been wonderful hearing from all the Members.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: As we move as one towards the digital future, I like to take this opportunity to thank the entire MCI family – our Minister, our Senior Ministers of State, everyone here – for their support and to include also the officers from the SNDGG.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
